Exposure (child-weeks) per cluster is 2500 in both arms
Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation applies, including additive one-cluster correction

The additive one-cluster correction adjusts for discreteness in small cluster samples

answer.summary: Using the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation with additive one-cluster correction, 4 clusters per arm are required to achieve 90% power (two-sided, α=0.05) to detect a difference between treatment rate 0.005 and control rate 0.010 per child-week, with 2500 child-weeks exposure per cluster, between-cluster CV of 0.15, and equal allocation. The design achieves 97.91% power at k=4; the preceding design (k=3) achieves 93.33% power.
answer.method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation with additive one-cluster correction. For Poisson-gamma heterogeneous count data, the variance of the log rate difference is computed as: Var(ΔlogRate) = [Poisson variance component] × [heterogeneity inflation factor], where the Poisson variance is (1/μ₀ + 1/μ₁) with μ₀=25 (control expected count) and μ₁=12.5 (treatment expected count), and the inflation factor is 1 + CV² × (μ₀ + μ₁)/(μ₀μ₁) = 1.0027. The continuous sample size is k = (z_{α/2} + z_β)² × Var(ΔlogRate) / (logRate)² = 2.631. The integer solution applies ceiling rounding (k=3) followed by an additive one-cluster correction (k_final=4).

Between-cluster coefficient of variation is constant at 0.15 across treatment and control arms

Two-sided test with significance level α = 0.05 (critical value z_{α/2} = 1.960)
Equal allocation to treatment and control (1:1)
The cluster-rate CV approximation formula applies, including the additive one-cluster correction for discrete designs
Tests are based on log-rate differences in a Wald-type framework with normal approximation
limitations: The approximation assumes large enough expected counts per cluster (μ₀=25, μ₁=12.5) for normal approximation validity; extreme imbalance could reduce accuracy
The between-cluster CV is assumed known and homogeneous; misspecification would affect actual power
No attrition, non-compliance, or exposure variability is incorporated
The formula uses a large-sample approximation; small-sample properties not directly assessed
Design assumes balanced cluster sizes and no missing exposure data
The additive one-cluster correction is heuristic; it improves discrete coverage but is not a formal continuity correction

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation for count data
# with additive one-cluster correction
# 
# Reference: Raudenbush & Liu (2001) and related cluster randomized trial designs
# for count outcomes with gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) heterogeneity.
#
# Design parameters
lambda_0 <- 0.010  # control rate (per child-week)
lambda_1 <- 0.005  # treatment rate (per child-week)
exposure <- 2500   # child-weeks per cluster
cv <- 0.15         # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05      # two-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.90
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)   # power critical value

# Expected counts per cluster under each arm
mu_0 <- lambda_0 * exposure  # control
mu_1 <- lambda_1 * exposure  # treatment

cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("  Control rate (λ₀):", lambda_0, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Treatment rate (λ₁):", lambda_1, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster:", exposure, "child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV:", cv, "\n")
cat("  Expected count per cluster (control):", mu_0, "\n")
cat("  Expected count per cluster (treatment):", mu_1, "\n")
cat("  Test: two-sided, α =", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  z_{α/2} =", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("  z_{power} =", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV approximation formula
# For comparing two cluster-level count rates with gamma-Poisson heterogeneity:
#
# Variance of log rate difference involves:
#  1. Poisson variance (1/μ_0 + 1/μ_1)
#  2. Gamma heterogeneity inflation: 1 + cv² * (μ_0 + μ_1) / (μ_0 * μ_1)
#
# Sample size formula (clusters per arm):
# k = (z_{α/2} + z_β)² * [Var(ΔlogRate) per cluster] / (logRate)²
#
# With the additive one-cluster correction: k_final = max(k_approx) + 1

# Variance components for Poisson part
var_poisson <- (1/mu_0) + (1/mu_1)

# Gamma heterogeneity variance inflation factor
# The between-cluster CV applies to the rate heterogeneity
inflation_factor <- 1 + (cv^2) * ((mu_0 + mu_1) / (mu_0 * mu_1))

# Total variance of log rate difference per cluster
var_log_rate_diff <- var_poisson * inflation_factor

# Log rate difference
log_rate_ratio <- log(lambda_1 / lambda_0)
effect_size <- log_rate_ratio

cat("Effect and Variance:\n")
cat("  Log(λ₁/λ₀) =", effect_size, "\n")
cat("  |Log rate ratio|:", abs(effect_size), "\n")
cat("  Poisson variance component (1/μ₀ + 1/μ₁):", var_poisson, "\n")
cat("  Heterogeneity inflation factor:", inflation_factor, "\n")
cat("  Total variance of log rate difference:", var_log_rate_diff, "\n\n")

# Sample size calculation (clusters per arm, continuous)
k_continuous <- ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * var_log_rate_diff) / (effect_size^2)

cat("Sample Size Calculation (Continuous):\n")
cat("  k = (z_{α/2} + z_β)² * Var(ΔlogRate) / (logRate)²\n")
cat("  k = (", z_alpha, "+", z_beta, ")² * ", var_log_rate_diff, " / ", 
    abs(effect_size)^2, "\n")
cat("  k = ", k_continuous, " clusters per arm (continuous)\n\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction
k_before_rounding <- k_continuous
k_rounded <- ceiling(k_continuous)
k_with_correction <- k_rounded + 1

cat("Rounding and One-Cluster Correction:\n")
cat("  Continuous solution: k =", k_before_rounding, "\n")
cat("  After ceiling: k =", k_rounded, "\n")
cat("  After additive one-cluster correction: k =", k_with_correction, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# Verify achieved power at the selected design (k = k_with_correction clusters)
# ============================================================================

# At k clusters per arm, the test statistic under the alternative is:
# Z = log_rate_ratio / sqrt(Var_log_rate_diff / k)
# Power = P(Z > z_{α/2} | H_1)

z_test_selected <- abs(effect_size) / sqrt(var_log_rate_diff / k_with_correction)
power_selected <- pnorm(z_test_selected - z_alpha)

cat("Verification at Selected Design (k =", k_with_correction, " clusters per arm):\n")
cat("  Test statistic Z =", z_test_selected, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power =", power_selected, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# Verify power at the preceding admissible design
# ============================================================================

k_preceding <- k_with_correction - 1
z_test_preceding <- abs(effect_size) / sqrt(var_log_rate_diff / k_preceding)
power_preceding <- pnorm(z_test_preceding - z_alpha)

cat("Verification at Preceding Design (k =", k_preceding, " clusters per arm):\n")
cat("  Test statistic Z =", z_test_preceding, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power =", power_preceding, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# Summary and Results
# ============================================================================

cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("FINAL RESULT:\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("Study Design: Cluster Randomized Trial (count outcomes, Poisson-Gamma)\n")
cat("Method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation\n")
cat("        with additive one-cluster correction\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Sample Size (Primary Result):\n")
cat("  Clusters per arm: ", k_with_correction, "\n")
cat("  Total clusters: ", 2 * k_with_correction, "\n")
cat("  Total child-weeks: ", 2 * k_with_correction * exposure, "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("  Treatment rate: ", lambda_1, " per child-week\n")
cat("  Control rate: ", lambda_0, " per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster: ", exposure, " child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV: ", cv, "\n")
cat("  Significance level: ", alpha, " (two-sided)\n")
cat("  Target power: ", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio (T:C): 1:1\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Achieved Power:\n")
cat("  At k = ", k_with_correction, ": ", round(power_selected, 4), "\n")
cat("  At k = ", k_preceding, ": ", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_with_correction, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_selected, 6), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 6), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * k_with_correction, unit = "clusters"),
      list(metric = "total_child_weeks", value = 2 * k_with_correction * exposure, unit = "child-weeks"),
      list(metric = "effect_size_log_rate_ratio", value = round(effect_size, 6), unit = "log scale"),
      list(metric = "variance_log_rate_diff", value = round(var_log_rate_diff, 6), unit = "per cluster"),
      list(metric = "heterogeneity_inflation_factor", value = round(inflation_factor, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_before_rounding, 6), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat(result_json, "\n")

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation for count data
# with additive one-cluster correction
# 
# Reference: Raudenbush & Liu (2001) and related cluster randomized trial designs
# for count outcomes with gamma-Poisson (negative binomial) heterogeneity.
#
# Design parameters
lambda_0 <- 0.010  # control rate (per child-week)
lambda_1 <- 0.005  # treatment rate (per child-week)
exposure <- 2500   # child-weeks per cluster
cv <- 0.15         # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05      # two-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.90
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)   # power critical value

# Expected counts per cluster under each arm
mu_0 <- lambda_0 * exposure  # control
mu_1 <- lambda_1 * exposure  # treatment

cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("  Control rate (λ₀):", lambda_0, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Treatment rate (λ₁):", lambda_1, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster:", exposure, "child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV:", cv, "\n")
cat("  Expected count per cluster (control):", mu_0, "\n")
cat("  Expected count per cluster (treatment):", mu_1, "\n")
cat("  Test: two-sided, α =", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  z_{α/2} =", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("  z_{power} =", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV approximation formula
# For comparing two cluster-level count rates with gamma-Poisson heterogeneity:
#
# Variance of log rate difference involves:
#  1. Poisson variance (1/μ_0 + 1/μ_1)
#  2. Gamma heterogeneity inflation: 1 + cv² * (μ_0 + μ_1) / (μ_0 * μ_1)
#
# Sample size formula (clusters per arm):
# k = (z_{α/2} + z_β)² * [Var(ΔlogRate) per cluster] / (logRate)²
#
# With the additive one-cluster correction: k_final = max(k_approx) + 1

# Variance components for Poisson part
var_poisson <- (1/mu_0) + (1/mu_1)

# Gamma heterogeneity variance inflation factor
# The between-cluster CV applies to the rate heterogeneity
inflation_factor <- 1 + (cv^2) * ((mu_0 + mu_1) / (mu_0 * mu_1))

# Total variance of log rate difference per cluster
var_log_rate_diff <- var_poisson * inflation_factor

# Log rate difference
log_rate_ratio <- log(lambda_1 / lambda_0)
effect_size <- log_rate_ratio

cat("Effect and Variance:\n")
cat("  Log(λ₁/λ₀) =", effect_size, "\n")
cat("  |Log rate ratio|:", abs(effect_size), "\n")
cat("  Poisson variance component (1/μ₀ + 1/μ₁):", var_poisson, "\n")
cat("  Heterogeneity inflation factor:", inflation_factor, "\n")
cat("  Total variance of log rate difference:", var_log_rate_diff, "\n\n")

# Sample size calculation (clusters per arm, continuous)
k_continuous <- ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * var_log_rate_diff) / (effect_size^2)

cat("Sample Size Calculation (Continuous):\n")
cat("  k = (z_{α/2} + z_β)² * Var(ΔlogRate) / (logRate)²\n")
cat("  k = (", z_alpha, "+", z_beta, ")² * ", var_log_rate_diff, " / ", 
    abs(effect_size)^2, "\n")
cat("  k = ", k_continuous, " clusters per arm (continuous)\n\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction
k_before_rounding <- k_continuous
k_rounded <- ceiling(k_continuous)
k_with_correction <- k_rounded + 1

cat("Rounding and One-Cluster Correction:\n")
cat("  Continuous solution: k =", k_before_rounding, "\n")
cat("  After ceiling: k =", k_rounded, "\n")
cat("  After additive one-cluster correction: k =", k_with_correction, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# Verify achieved power at the selected design (k = k_with_correction clusters)
# ============================================================================

# At k clusters per arm, the test statistic under the alternative is:
# Z = log_rate_ratio / sqrt(Var_log_rate_diff / k)
# Power = P(Z > z_{α/2} | H_1)

z_test_selected <- abs(effect_size) / sqrt(var_log_rate_diff / k_with_correction)
power_selected <- pnorm(z_test_selected - z_alpha)

cat("Verification at Selected Design (k =", k_with_correction, " clusters per arm):\n")
cat("  Test statistic Z =", z_test_selected, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power =", power_selected, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# Verify power at the preceding admissible design
# ============================================================================

k_preceding <- k_with_correction - 1
z_test_preceding <- abs(effect_size) / sqrt(var_log_rate_diff / k_preceding)
power_preceding <- pnorm(z_test_preceding - z_alpha)

cat("Verification at Preceding Design (k =", k_preceding, " clusters per arm):\n")
cat("  Test statistic Z =", z_test_preceding, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power =", power_preceding, "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# Summary and Results
# ============================================================================

cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("FINAL RESULT:\n")
cat("================================================================================\n")
cat("Study Design: Cluster Randomized Trial (count outcomes, Poisson-Gamma)\n")
cat("Method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation\n")
cat("        with additive one-cluster correction\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Sample Size (Primary Result):\n")
cat("  Clusters per arm: ", k_with_correction, "\n")
cat("  Total clusters: ", 2 * k_with_correction, "\n")
cat("  Total child-weeks: ", 2 * k_with_correction * exposure, "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("  Treatment rate: ", lambda_1, " per child-week\n")
cat("  Control rate: ", lambda_0, " per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster: ", exposure, " child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV: ", cv, "\n")
cat("  Significance level: ", alpha, " (two-sided)\n")
cat("  Target power: ", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio (T:C): 1:1\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Achieved Power:\n")
cat("  At k = ", k_with_correction, ": ", round(power_selected, 4), "\n")
cat("  At k = ", k_preceding, ": ", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_with_correction, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_selected, 6), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 6), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * k_with_correction, unit = "clusters"),
      list(metric = "total_child_weeks", value = 2 * k_with_correction * exposure, unit = "child-weeks"),
      list(metric = "effect_size_log_rate_ratio", value = round(effect_size, 6), unit = "log scale"),
      list(metric = "variance_log_rate_diff", value = round(var_log_rate_diff, 6), unit = "per cluster"),
      list(metric = "heterogeneity_inflation_factor", value = round(inflation_factor, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_before_rounding, 6), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat(result_json, "\n")
